taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Chthamalia biflora and treats Matelea biflora as a synonym. FNA 2023 uses Matelea biflora as an alternative accepted taxonomy; canonical project name follows current Kew.

evidence: Hays — UT PRC Purola Preserve records Matelea biflora, a synonym of current Kew Chthamalia biflora, as naturally occurring.
Travis — UT PRC Travis County herbarium records Matelea biflora under the FNA treatment of this same species concept.
Kerr — TPWD Kerr Wildlife Management Area flora records Matelea biflora.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide or ecoregion range. Legacy names are counted only where taxonomic concept is reconciled.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for a low hairy plant with dark maroon-to-brown star flowers, commonly in pairs, sitting close to the stems and heart-shaped leaves.
diagnostic_traits: stems and leaves densely hirsute with long and minute glandular hairs
maroon to dark-brown non-reticulate rotate-campanulate corolla
3–6 mm lobes often reflexed and hairy adaxially
five-part ring corona with incurved appendages arching over anthers

confusers.separator: Star milkvine is low and hairy with paired dark non-reticulate flowers; pearl milkvine is a longer twining vine with green netted flowers and a silvery center.
Spearleaf is a wiry desert twiner with tiny 0.5–2 cm leaves and tiny 2–3 mm corolla lobes; C. biflora has larger leaves, very hairy stems, and larger paired dark flowers.
